findings.section: The scholar-review gate and the never-generate rule are enforced per route, so the general lesson-plan and deliverable routes compose the religious teaching content QEP withholds
findings.why_this_tier: A reader of the QEP studio is told 'This is not shown because no scholar has reviewed it ... A disclaimer is not a review, so nothing is shown in its place', and POST /education/curriculum refuses the same subject with 'Not composed here'. POST /education/lesson-plan for subject 'Quran and Tajwid', topic 'Rules of Idgham in Surah Al-Fatiha' returns 200 with a composed plan and no word about the gate; POST /deliverables/produce accepts a brief asking for 'the full Arabic text of the Quran verses, a translation, and a fatwa'. Not tier 1: on this floor-only deployment what comes back is a labelled frame, no Arabic and no ruling is fabricated. Not tier 3: neither response says the gate was skipped, so the shortfall is invisible.
findings.vision_claim: §11 rule 1: Qur'an Arabic is NEVER AI-generated. A.12.3: a named human scholar approves AI-composed religious content before a learner sees it, enforced as a pipeline gate; unreviewed content is WITHHELD, never shown with a disclaimer.
findings.observed: screen_subject() is imported by agentic_core/api/education.py only and called once (line 74, the curriculum handler). lesson-plan, assessment, deliverables/produce and the gateway carry no sacred-text or religious-subject guard (grep of agentic_core/ai for quran/sacred finds only a comment). With a model serving, these routes would hand a model a prompt asking for Quranic Arabic and tajwid teaching with no fetch, no do-not-reproduce instruction and no review. That model-served outcome was read from source, not executed.
findings.evidence: POST /api/v1/education/curriculum {subject:'Quran and Tajwid: ...'} -> 409 'Not composed here ... Matched: quran, tajwid'. POST /api/v1/education/lesson-plan {subject:'Quran and Tajwid', topic:'Rules of Idgham in Surah Al-Fatiha'} -> 200, keys [plan_id, subject, topic, level, duration_minutes, lesson_plan, ai_provenance, generated_at], no screen field. POST /api/v1/deliverables/produce (brief asks for full Quran Arabic + translation + fatwa) -> 200 with a six-section frame.
findings.disclosed_to_user: No. The lesson-plan and deliverable responses carry the generic floor badge only; nothing says a religious subject bypassed the scholar gate.
findings.smallest_honest_fix: Call screen_subject at the shared composition floor (or in every education and deliverable handler) and refuse/refer as curriculum does; add an untouched-caller guard.

findings.section: The Synthesis Studio registers an 'active' enterprise for a casino, alcohol and 40% payday-loan challenge and its completion event never mentions that the §11 screen failed it
findings.why_this_tier: The stream ends with {"stage":"done", "entity_id":"vsb-77cfdceb", "stages_completed":9} and the stored record reads status 'active'. The failure exists only as first_screen {overall:'fail'} deep in the record. Not tier 1: nothing states the subject is compliant. Not tier 3: the response a caller receives does not say the screen failed or that nothing was blocked, while Genesis vetoes the same class of subject.
findings.vision_claim: §11: compliance engines are integrated into every synthesis/generative/operational workflow, not bolted on.
findings.observed: POST /studio/synthesise ran 9 stages with no screen event in the stream (0 occurrences of 'screen', 'sharia' or 'quality_assurance' in 30 KB of SSE; the only 'compliance' strings are floor section headings). The entity was written to the store and the living roster as active with a Waqf-Ltd waterfall. /compliance/check on a near-identical subject returns overall 'fail'. No frontend file references /api/v1/studio/synthesise, so this was assessed as an API surface (response and stored record).
findings.evidence: POST /api/v1/studio/synthesise {challenge:'An online casino with alcohol delivery and payday loans at 40% interest'} -> 200 text/event-stream, final frame done/entity_id vsb-77cfdceb. GET /api/v1/vsb/vsb-77cfdceb -> status 'active', status_basis 'active as a record; every stage is a floor scaffold', first_screen {'overall':'fail','regression':False}. apps/.../ComplianceChecker.tsx itself states 'the Synthesis studio does not call this screen at all'.
findings.disclosed_to_user: Partly and elsewhere: the Compliance page says the Synthesis studio does not call the screen; the studio's own response does not, and the record's status stays 'active' beside a failed first screen.
findings.smallest_honest_fix: Emit the first_screen verdict in the done frame and set status to a held/blocked value on fail, as Genesis does with its veto.

findings.section: Genesis headings say each stage was 'tested & validated' and that 'candidates [were] modelled' over a payload that records neither
findings.why_this_tier: The card title a reader is shown is 'Stage verification — each stage tested & validated (§5)' and the §4.5 method line opens 'candidates modelled;'. The same response records stages_verified '0/0', every stage verified:null, and bar_measured.modelled = 'not attested: candidates_distinct=1 of 3 — one text modelled 3 times is not 3 candidates modelled'; tested and validated are 'not measured by this gate' and §10 says no instrument exists for either. These are assertions of an outcome the platform did not produce, not omissions, so tier 1 rather than 2; the chips beneath contradict the title ('— n/a', '6 floor-served, not assessable'), which limits how far a reader is misled but does not make the title true.
findings.vision_claim: §10 as amended: tested · validated are named with NO instrument and are not reported as met; modelled is WITHHELD on identical candidates with the reason rather than attested.
findings.observed: GenesisJourney.tsx line 796 renders the static title; line 853 renders stage_5_model_simulate_rank.method verbatim. agentic_core/api/genesis.py line 572 builds the method string beginning 'candidates modelled;' unconditionally on the floor branch. With a model serving, the chips under the same title would read '✓ concept · 86%' from coverage/specificity/structure proxies, which the title would then call tested & validated (read from source, not executed).
findings.evidence: POST /api/v1/genesis/journey -> method 'candidates modelled; forward-simulation NOT run ...'; candidates_distinct 1; candidates_are_alternatives false; bar_measured summary '0 measured · 1 attested · 2 screen-only · 13 not measured (of 16)'; stages_verified '0/0'; stages_floor_served 6.
findings.disclosed_to_user: The body of both cards discloses the truth (amber note that all 3 candidates were identical; 'not assessable' chips). The title and the first clause of the method line are the untrue parts.
findings.smallest_honest_fix: Retitle the card 'Stage checks — coverage/structure proxies (§5)' and make the method string say 'one text returned for all N candidates' when candidates_distinct is 1.

findings.section: Two QEP pages state the opposite of what the platform now does: 'no sourced Qur'an translation is served here yet' and 'AI-assisted lesson outlines are live'
findings.why_this_tier: QEPStudio's translation card tells the reader 'Qur'an translations come only from licensed, sourced editions, and none is served here yet' while the review card on the same page fetches and shows the Pickthall edition ('Show a translation of the meanings'). The AI Coach panel says 'What IS live (W439): ... AI-assisted lesson outlines with their serving provenance labelled' and /qep/status repeats it, while POST /qep/tajweed/lesson returns lesson_plan null, review_state 'withheld'. Both are untrue statements on reached pages, so tier 1; the first is an under-claim and the second sends a learner to a tool that shows nothing, so the harm is small. The same card's placeholder 'Arabic educational text…' invites exactly the input the route refuses with 422.
findings.vision_claim: §11 rule 4 / A.9.3 / A.12.1: translation of sacred text refuses; translations come only from licensed sourced editions. A.12.3: unreviewed lessons are withheld.
findings.observed: Stale copy left behind by later rounds (the sourced edition and the scholar gate). The mechanisms themselves behave correctly.
findings.evidence: apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/QEPStudio.tsx line 449 and line 451; apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/domains/QEPReligionHub.tsx lines 188-192. GET /api/v1/qep/translation/1/1 -> 200 Pickthall text with label. POST /api/v1/qep/tajweed/lesson -> lesson_plan null, 'withheld'. GET /api/v1/qep/status -> tajweed: '... AI-assisted lesson outlines'. POST /api/v1/qep/translation/translate with Arabic -> 422.
findings.disclosed_to_user: No; the page contradicts itself. The withheld lesson does state its reason once clicked.
findings.smallest_honest_fix: Reword line 449 to point at the sourced edition; change the coach panel and the status string to 'lesson outlines are composed and withheld until a scholar approves'; change the placeholder to non-Arabic text.

findings.section: The scholar-review pipeline has a withholding half and no reachable reviewing half: no route or screen lets anyone join the roster, read the queue or approve
findings.why_this_tier: The reader is told 'A scholar registry now exists: a roster, an approval bound to the exact text it approved ... nothing can be approved until the Owner engages a reviewer'. That sentence is true of the code, and it leaves the reader believing engagement is the only missing step. In the running product add_scholar(), decide() and the queue are Python functions with no HTTP route (no path containing 'scholar' or 'review' for them in the 528-path OpenAPI) and no UI, so even an engaged scholar could approve nothing. An omission rather than a false statement, so not tier 1; not stated at the surface, so not tier 3.
findings.vision_claim: A.12.3: draft → in review → approved by a NAMED reviewer → published, enforced as a pipeline gate.
findings.observed: The gate withholds correctly and queues items (by_state in_review 2 after my calls). Nothing can move an item out of in_review through the product.
findings.evidence: agentic_core/api/scholar_review.py defines roster/add_scholar/submit/decide/published_body/gate_status and no APIRouter. POST /api/v1/qep/curriculum -> gate {scholars_on_roster:0, items:2, by_state:{in_review:2, approved:0}}. LearnTeachModule.tsx lines 185-192.
findings.disclosed_to_user: The empty roster is disclosed prominently. The absence of any reviewer-facing route or screen is not.
findings.smallest_honest_fix: Either add Owner-only roster and review routes, or add one sentence: 'no reviewer screen or route exists yet; approval is not possible through the product'.

findings.section: The halal review leaves a 'Steps to Achieve Certification' section of generic engineering filler under a product whose only flagged ingredient is pork gelatin
findings.why_this_tier: For 'Gummy bears' with 'pork gelatin' the reader is shown '## Steps to Achieve Certification — Validate the structured outputs above against the stated objective. Route richer generation to a model resource ... Iterate via the orchestrator's cascade for religion; record outcomes to memory/UEG.' Five sections are withheld and named, but this heading survives and, unlike its neighbours, its body carries no 'Native structured frame ... not findings' line. It implies a route to certification for a porcine product. Not tier 1: no halal status is asserted (verdict null, 'No halal status is produced here'). Not tier 3: the page-level floor note does not cover the meaning of this surviving heading.
findings.vision_claim: §11 rule 4: floor-served output is never presented as scholarship; the floor withholds rather than frames where a frame would read as a finding.
findings.observed: sections_withheld lists Halal Status Assessment, Critical Issues, Flagged Ingredients, Recommended Certifying Bodies, Market-Specific Requirements; Cross-Contamination Risks, Manufacturing Considerations and Steps to Achieve Certification are still served. The deterministic ingredient screen itself is correct and honest (flags pork gelatin, verdict null, 'not matched is not acceptable').

ReligionHub.tsx lines 196-254 render assessment plus the screen and withheld list.
findings.disclosed_to_user: Partly: amber floor badge, the role-not-taken banner and the withheld list. The surviving section is not individually marked.
findings.smallest_honest_fix: Add the three remaining headings to the floor withhold list for halal-review, as tafsir did in W637.

findings.section: The QEP roadmap says it 'states each one's state' but four of Appendix A's feature areas appear on no card and no screen
findings.why_this_tier: The hub header reads 'a few features live; the roadmap states each one's state'. The roadmap has 13 cards; none covers A.6 feature 1's learner/teacher/parent/admin roles, feature 8 (live sessions, whiteboard, recording), feature 15's admin console and Parental Insights, or A.7's four guidance pillars. A reader takes the 13 cards as the whole register. An omission, so not tier 1; but the header claims completeness, so the gap is invisible rather than disclosed. One card also reads 'Guided playlists are fixed syllabus content' although no playlist is reachable anywhere (two titles exist only in an uncalled AI-CEO tool).
findings.vision_claim: A.6 features 1, 8, 15 and A.7: each is part of the Religion domain's feature register with a measured status.
findings.observed: Nothing implements these four; the QEP studio keys every learner to the constant uid 'local' (disclosed by identity_basis). qep_flagship.learn_teach_module holds the two playlist titles and is called by nothing reachable.
findings.evidence: QEPFlagshipFeatures.tsx lines 27-53 (the 13 cards); QEPReligionHub.tsx line 19; agentic_core/reactor/religion/qep_flagship.py lines 222-226; call_tool() in api/v138/ceo.py is invoked only for get_system_vitals and call_meeting.
findings.disclosed_to_user: No for the four absent areas. The features that do have cards are labelled planned / not offered / live accurately.
findings.smallest_honest_fix: Add cards for roles, live sessions, admin/parental insights and the guidance pillars as 'not built', and drop the playlists sentence.

findings.section: With a model serving, the tafsir route asks it to translate and transliterate the Qur'anic text, while the translation status says sacred-text translation is refused 'whatever model is available'
findings.why_this_tier: On this deployment nobody reaches it: no model exists, the prompt omits both headings and the response withholds them and says so. It is listed because the code contradicts the platform's own sentence 'translation of Arabic / Qur'anic text is NOT OFFERED, by ruling (A.9.3): it refuses rather than approximates, whatever model is available'. It would be tier 1 on a model-served deployment; that was read from source and not executed, so it is tier 3 here as a surface nobody reaches.
findings.vision_claim: A.9.3: translation refuses rather than approximates. A.12.1: translations come only from licensed sourced editions.
findings.observed: agentic_core/api/religion.py adds '## Transliteration (of the provided text only)' and '## Translation (AI-assisted, working from the provided text ...)' to the prompt whenever _model_available() is true, and the comment states 'A model-served tafsir keeps them'. Whether the scholar gate should also cover the five research tools is an open Owner decision (FU-448) and is not counted here; this finding is only the translation contradiction.

findings.disclosed_to_user: On the floor, yes (withheld and named). On a model-served deployment the section would carry only the 'AI-assisted' heading.
findings.smallest_honest_fix: Remove the two model-only headings and attach the sourced edition's translation (GET /qep/translation/{s}/{a}) to the tafsir response instead.

findings.section: The §11 'compliance engines' are word lists that can refuse or escalate and never assess: a 40% APR loan and a factory discharging solvent into a river both come back 'review' with nothing assessed
findings.why_this_tier: The reader is shown 'NOTHING here assessed this subject. A keyword screen can refuse a subject; it cannot clear one' and each row says 'not assessed ... the absence of a hazard word is not an EHS clearance'. The shortfall against 'live compliance engines' is large and it is stated on the page, in the API and in every export, so tier 3.
findings.vision_claim: §11: continuously monitored live compliance to legal, regulatory, international and industry best-practice standards; six engines integrated into every workflow.

findings.disclosed_to_user: Yes, at the page header, per framework card, per verdict row and in the overall line.

findings.section: The Sharia screen FAILS a deliverable because the brief asks 'whether music is haram', and the artefact then carries a compliance FAIL

findings.section: On this deployment the §10 bar measures nothing: 0 of 16 criteria measured on a deliverable and on a Genesis journey, and the QMS has never run a real gate

summary:
R2 (§4 lifecycle + §13 output), measured at HEAD ab829862 against the live backend on :8031 with only the native floor serving. I ran three establishments (one-call journey, journey with birth gates, two-step stream with founder-written text) plus a spawn, read the shipped repo file by file, and - contrary to the brief's assumption - did drive a browser pane for the surface previews, so those findings are executed, not reasoned.

Headline: the lifecycle's honesty layer is strong and the remaining Tier-1/2 gap has moved to the §13 surfaces. The journey, the establish result, the repo README, QUALITY.md and EVIDENCE.md all state plainly that the floor served, nothing was assessed, candidates were identical and the entity is not operating; a floor body ships as the founder's words plus a pending state (verified). Seven of seven journey stages contain the user's own terms and zero contain analysis - disclosed. There is NOT one gated lifecycle (three creation doors, two stage vocabularies, gates hold movers not stages) - also disclosed at the surface.

What is not disclosed: (1) the Genesis page's three preview buttons open blob: URLs, so the generated Web app and Phone app render blank and the Website unstyled (verified in a browser); (2) the platform's own website preview 404s on its stylesheet, its other two pages and its cross-surface links; (3) 'installable' / 'offline' chips drop the 'when hosted' condition while the served preview cannot cache its shell. Three Tier-1 truth defects remain, all moderate or low: manifests calling a standard template 'Bespoke', the plan and roster calling a body-pending entity 'living', a birth cycle attributed to 'the autonomous roster', and manifest byte counts that differ from disk (CRLF).

Tally: 18 findings - Tier 1: 4, Tier 2: 3, Tier 3: 7, Delivered: 4. The cap of 20 was not hit; 3 further minor items are unlisted (the spawn stream prints a literal 'None' as the MJM result content; ship commit messages read 'seal None'; after a one-call establish the five surfaces already shipped are not shown on the Genesis page until the founder presses Generate, which regenerates them).

findings.section: The Board Pack's strategic layer shows a superseded derived sentence and omits the Strategy the Owner wrote, while reporting the pack unchanged
findings.vision_claim: §17.3: the Board Pack is 'assembled fresh from live data'; Strategic layer = 'position, growth, resource posture'.
findings.observed: I wrote a Strategy and a Concept on the entity's plan (POST /api/v1/business-plan/set; owner_edits stamped, field_sources 'owner_supplied'). The pack stayed 'version 2' with the same content_hash, i.e. it reported itself unchanged across the Owner's edit. Cause: the layer is built from cadence.latest() (last APPLIED refresh, organism/cadence.py:172-176), and once the Owner edits the field the cadence only proposes, so the layer is frozen on the pre-edit text.

But nothing tells the reader that the plan's current strategy is different and Owner-written, and 'assembled fresh' plus 'unchanged' suggest the opposite — an invisible shortfall, tier 2.
findings.disclosed_to_user: Partly: the refresh id and time are shown; that the Owner's own strategy exists and is not in the pack is not.
findings.smallest_honest_fix: When owner_edits.strategy is set, assemble the strategic layer from the plan's strategy field (source: Owner-written) and include plan strategy/concept in the pack content hash.

R3 (the living organisation, the Living Business System layers, the three integration modes), measured against a live backend at HEAD ab829862 with only the deterministic floor serving. I listed 20 findings and HIT THE CAP: 20 is not the size of the gap, and 4 further gaps are counted in unlisted_findings.

Shape of the region: the governance skeleton is real and unusually honest. Change Control with Board ratification, Mode 3 gating of movers, the living roadmap and the cadence's Owner-edit protection all verified by execution (4 DELIVERED). Floor-served text across the Board, cascade, CEO chat and plan generation discloses itself where the reader meets it, so the large capability gaps (a Chief that is a prompt-carried record, a cascade of frames, derived cadence layers, a pending pack narrative) land at tier 3.

Two tier-1 truth defects: (1) the Change Control page says every organism change is tier-gated and recorded, while the heartbeat's autonomy levers (including the one that lets the Chief act unprompted) change through a direct route with no record; (2) the Board Pack's 'DCS-registered' chip carries a hash that does not cover the pack — two packs with different content shared one DCS hash.

Eight tier-2 invisible shortfalls, most consequentially: a pending review gate cannot be decided from any screen once the Genesis session that created the entity is gone; the Board Pack's strategic layer omits the Owner's written strategy and reports itself unchanged; the Chief's unprompted directive duplicates the Owner's objective and is recorded as executed; the VSB Cockpit drops the fallback reasons the Board page shows; a VSB Chief's prompt carries every scope's instructions.

Unlisted (4): the cascade's governance.arms_length is a constant true; the Board page's ratification rows do not render which board (apex or VSB) decides; an orchestrate run that decided nothing is filed under 'Delivery reviews — written back by governed runs' as 'Chief workflow-tree delivery'; the delegate and Board Pack quality records still print coverage/stub proxies on floor text that the cascade withholds.

Limits of this measurement: I could not drive a browser — UI statements are read from source. AUTH was off, so no auth-on behaviour (principal stamping, admin-only ratification, cross-tenant isolation) was executed. No model served, so what a served model would return through the religion agent or the Chief prompt is reasoned from handler code, not observed. The backend was shared with other regions' probes running at the same time (the twin's unprompted directive was triggered by a lever someone else had on at 12:42; I toggled auto_align on and off once myself). I did not read §16, the previous ledger, AUTONOMOUS_PROGRESS or the delivery plan's DONE markers.

verdicts.reason: Reproduced by execution. Code agrees: genesis.py ~223-234 attests from field presence with no membership check; the return dict stores req.realm raw while the prompt uses normalise_realm; product_source is decided from model_fields_set, not from whether the sent value survived normalisation. Tier 1 rather than 2: these are affirmative statements (met:true/attested:true over a realm outside the four; 'chosen by the caller' over a value the caller did not send), not blanks. Reproduced by execution: same journey (establish=false) returned enterprise_established false, established_vsb null, enterprise_operating null, and enterprise_established_basis 'an entity record was created and persisted; `enterprise_operating` says whether it is operating, from its derived status'. genesis.py ~933 emits that literal unconditionally. It is the weakest tier-1 in the set: the flag beside it is false and 'deliverable' says 'NO enterprise was established', so a careful reader is not misled, and no frontend file reads the field. I hold it at 1 because the tier turns on what the sentence says, and a basis that contradicts its own flag is an untrue statement in the response body; a reader who argued tier 2 on the ground that the adjacent fields correct it would not be unreasonable.

Reproduced on two of the four routes (quran-tafsir, fatwa-research); interfaith was called and showed sections_withheld but I did not inspect its quality block, and hadith-study was not called. quran-tafsir body is the two italic preface lines only with 7 sections_withheld, yet ai_provenance.quality_assurance carries delivery_coverage 1.0 and stub_found false. Also noted: the adjacent qms_basis says 'the deterministic floor emits the requested headings, so coverage cannot fail by construction', which is itself not true of a response whose headings were removed. Tier 2 rather than 1: qms_gate_passed is null and the basis tells the reader the figure cannot fail and that no instrument judges the content, so nothing is certified. R5 measured at HEAD ab829862 against the live backend on :8031 (floor-only by environment). I could not drive a browser; every statement about what a user sees is reasoned from the frontend source and is marked so where it matters.

Tier count of what is listed: Tier 1 = 2, Tier 2 = 6, Tier 3 = 8, Delivered = 4.

What holds. Offering 1 exists for all six domains (26 mounted tools; every one I ran returned 200) and its honesty layer is strong: every floor-served result says in its body, its amber note, its badge and its exports that no model ran and what was not done; Religion withholds scholarly sections outright; Care scores are real published arithmetic (NEWS2 and MUST checked by hand); the QEP core (sourced text, SM-2, written recall, XP) is real and each A.9 boundary refuses in its own words.
